newsitem.title: USA: Antitrust review extended for Raytheon -WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Antitrust review extended for Raytheon -WSJ.

text.p: The Justice Department has extended for another month its antitrust review of Raytheon's proposed $3 billion acquisition of Texas Instruments' defense business, the Wall Street Journal said Friday.
The paper said executives familiar with the situation confirmed that Raytheon had agreed to an extension of the review, which was scheduled to expire today.
The report said the reasons for extending the review were not clear.
Raytheon is also seeking to acquire the defense holdings of General Motors' Hughes Electronics Corp after defeating Northrop Grumman with a $9.5 billion bid.
Friday's report quoted a Northrop spokesman as saying that his company is concerned about the Raytheon-Texas Instruments pact's effect on competition for making fighter jet radars.
After the acquisition, Raytheon will control the only two businesses now making microchips and other parts that are key to combat-aircraft radars, the paper said.

The paper said others following the deal believe Northrop is protesting the issue to regulators and that the only solution will be for either Raytheon or Texas Instruments to divest part of their businesses involved in radar components.
